item.title: ‘She Kills Monsters’ to be staged at Peninsula College
item.description: PORT ANGELES — The Peninsula College Drama Department will stage “She Kills Monsters” at 7 p.m. Fridays and Saturdays through March 14.

item.title: First Friday Art Walk set this weekend in Sequim
item.description: SEQUIM — The First Friday Art Walk will celebrate with a green-themed event from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m. Friday at various venues in downtown Sequim.

item.title: Studium General series to wrap up with talk on ‘Empathy’
item.description: PORT ANGELES — Janet Lucas will present “What We Talk About When We Talk About Empathy” at 12:35 p.m. Thursday.

item.title: Sequim proclamation attempts to lessen immigration concerns
item.description: SEQUIM — Following stories of federal immigration enforcement across the country and regular protests along city streets, Sequim Mayor Rachel Anderson shared a proclamation saying the city will serve and protect all community members regardless of immigration status.

item.title: Weekend spay/neuter clinic draws more than 150 animals
item.description: PORT ANGELES — Dr. Joel Cuthbert of Gig Harbor prepared a full-sized dog to be spayed with assistance from Dr. Laura Monahan of Sequim during a two-day clinic this weekend inside the Home Arts building at the Clallam County Fairgrounds.

item.title: Shipwright’s Regatta
item.description: The 35th annual Shipwright’s Regatta got underway on Port Townsend Bay on Saturday after it was postponed for a week due to dangerously high winds.

item.title: Crews temporarily fix leak in 30-inch pipe
item.description: Port Townsend declares state of emergency to deploy resources for repairs

item.description: Wrestling club registration and OJBR tryouts

item.title: All-NISQUALLY LEAGUE: Vailolo, O’Hara make first team
item.description: PORT TOWNSEND — East Jefferson’s Penina Vailolo and Luke O’Hara made the all-Nisqually League girls and boys first teams.
